title: Opaque ledgerization for admin events and residency-bound evidence automation
creator: Aisha Patel
description: Create a production-ready service that ledgerizes admin actions (console changes, RBAC grants, config toggles) into an append-only, residency-aware evidence stream. The stream must provide tamper-evident proofs, optional WORM storage handoff per customer region, and automated reporting exports that satisfy internal compliance auditors and external regulators. The goal is to deliver end-to-end evidence from event capture -> integrity proofing -> region-bound durable export with an operator-friendly UI and audit export API.
background: Customers operating in regulated regions require provable custody of admin actions and configuration changes. Current audit capture is fragmented: admin events are sparse across API gateway logs, console telemetry, and ad-hoc DB records. We need a unified ledger layer that can (1) centralize events, (2) create integrity anchors (hash chains / Merkle snapshots), and (3) support region-specific WORM handoff and automated evidence bundles for reviews and legal holds.
acceptance_criteria: All admin action types (console, API admin endpoints, role grants, config changes) are emitted to the ledger service within 30s of action
Ledger entries are immutable once sealed and include a cryptographic digest that can be verified independently
Per-customer residency policy evaluated at ingestion; exports to region-specific WORM sinks succeed or surface a clear, actionable error
Automated daily evidence bundles generated for customers with retention=legal_hold and stored for configured retention windows
Admin UI shows per-customer evidence chain status and last-sealed snapshot time
End-to-end integration test and a sample auditor report generation pipeline exist in the repo
in_scope: Design and implement ledger ingestion API and schema for admin events
Hash-chain / Merkle snapshot generator and attestation headers
Pluggable sink adapters for cloud WORM targets (S3 Object Lock, GCS retention, Azure immutable blobs)
Region-aware routing and policy evaluation at ingest time
Console dashboard to surface evidence health and export controls
CLI/HTTP export API for evidence bundles and legal holds
out_of_scope: Full-text search of historical audit events (analytics team will own)
Replacing existing runtime request logs used by incident responders
Long-term forensic analysis tooling (will be a separate product integration)
proposed_solution: Introduce a new 'ledger' microservice that accepts normalized admin events. Each event is written to an append-only store (rocksdb-backed commit log) and periodically sealed into snapshots. Sealing computes a Merkle root; the root is published to a signing service that issues a signed attestation. Snapshot manifests are then routed to a region-specific export worker which prepares a manifest and pushes to the configured WORM sink with retention metadata. For customers that require legal-hold exports, the worker will generate a signed evidence bundle (manifest + chunked objects + attestation) and optionally push to escrow storage or trigger the export API to the customer's S3 bucket. A lightweight console surface will show ingestion latency, last-sealed snapshot, and export status per region.
technical_notes: Use an append-only commit log with sequence numbers to facilitate resume and replay (consider NATS JetStream or Kafka for initial MVP)
RocksDB local cache for hot customer partitions; long-term store will be object blobs in regionally-located object storage
Sealing cadence: configurable per-customer, default 1 hour for high-volume tenants and 6 hours for low-volume
Attestation signing keys use KMS-backed keys; signing service must emit timestamped signatures and be rotatable
Export adapters will tag objects with residency and retention metadata required by cloud WORM features (S3 Object Lock mode, retention until date)
Design manifest format as a small JSON file with deterministic canonicalization for signature verification
Provide a verification CLI that can validate signed manifests against the public attestation key
rollout_plan: Phase 1 (MVP): Ingest + local sealing + signed snapshot API in staging. Test with internal compliance tenant.
Phase 2: Implement S3/GCS export adapters and per-region policy evaluation; run export trials to customer-managed test buckets.
Phase 3: Console UI + export scheduling + legal-hold bundle generation; run a soft-launch with three pilot customers.
Phase 4: Hardening, performance tuning, and security review; GA release behind a feature flag
monitoring_and_alerting: Ingestion lag metric (95th percentile) with alert if > 60s
Snapshot seal failures with SLO error budget burn dashboard
Export worker error rate per-region > 1% alert
Unsigned manifest anomalies (mismatch digest) critical pager
qa_steps: Synthetic test harness emits representative admin actions across regions and validates manifests and attestation signatures
Chaos test: simulate region outage, ensure per-customer residency policy prevents cross-region export
End-to-end test: generate evidence bundle and run verification CLI against public attestation key
Performance test: validate commit log scales to 10k events/min with median lat < 200ms
